caption:
4 children died in 24 hours. Nearly 100,000 suspected measles cases reported across Bangladesh.

Bangladesh has registered four more child deaths linked to measles symptoms within a single day, with 116 new cases confirmed in the same period.

According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), 93 people have died from confirmed measles cases since March 15, while 619 others with suspected symptoms have died.

The Dhaka Division has been the hardest hit, recording the highest number of symptomatic fatalities at 266.

Other regions including Rajshahi, Sylhet, Chattogram, Barishal, Mymensingh, Khulna, and Rangpur have also reported significant death tolls.

In the last 24 hours, 941 people sought hospital care for measles symptoms, with 889 requiring admission to hospitals.

Dhaka registered the highest caseload of hospitalisations, with 387 admissions in the latest daily count.

The DGHS stated that the cumulative number of suspected measles cases in the satuation stands at 99,207, while confirmed cases total 11,710.

Of the 82,844 patients hospitalised so far, 79,152 have been discharged after receiving treatment.

headline: High Court issues rule on bail of former CEC Habibul Awal
summary: The court has called for an explanation as to why the former Chief Election Commissioner should not be denied bail.
details: The High Court has issued a rule asking for the reason why former Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Habibul Awal should not be denied bail.
This legal action comes as the former CEC faces various allegations and legal challenges regarding his tenure and conduct.
The court's decision to issue a rule means it will now examine the arguments and the state's position on whether he should remain in custody.
The proceedings are part of a broader scrutiny of the previous administration's election commission and its impartiality.
caption:
Why should former CEC Habibul Awal be granted bail? The High Court is now demanding an answer.

The High Court has issued a rule asking for the reason why former Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Habibul Awal should not be denied bail.

This legal action comes as the former CEC faces various allegations and legal challenges regarding his tenure and conduct.

The court's decision to issue a rule means it will now examine the arguments and the state's position on whether he should remain in custody.

The proceedings are part of a broader scrutiny of the previous administration's election commission and its impartiality.
